pebble:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: actual production character-design candidate source atlas for a small 2D game, NOT a presentation mockup.
Create one landscape 3-column by 2-row atlas of SIX FULL-BODY CHARACTER DESIGNS, with real transparent background, no labels, no letters, no grid lines, no decorations. Each cell must contain one centered separate complete creature, with uniform baseline and matched body scale. Leave generous transparent gutters. Keep all six entire silhouettes inside their cells. Use the provided reference as the exact species identity and art-style authority: adorable tiny limbless creature, two round dark bead eyes, mouthless face, no arms or hands, tiny feet where present, simple soft painterly game-sprite shading, restrained details and large readable shapes. Preserve its proportions, facial placement, softness, front three-quarter view, dark thin outline, lighting and tactile paint style. THIS IS ORGANIC EVOLUTION, not creatures wearing equipment. All combat features must grow directly out of the body, with continuous tissue/material transitions, same shading and outline. NO weapons held or strapped, no handles, no metal hardware, no clothes, no belts, no floating artifacts, no sparkles or glow clouds, no realistic anatomy or horror. Each evolution must retain the same core creature and recognizable face at a 64px game scale. Do not include regeneration/healing designs. Read order row 1: original base creature, blade adaptation, piercing adaptation. Row 2: carapace adaptation, protective guard adaptation, secretion adaptation. Distinguish the functions through the species' own anatomy. These SIX drawings are the deliverable source assets, high-quality and ready to crop individually.
SPECIES: PEBBLE. Reference is the warm sandy ochre rounded angular pebble creature with two tiny tan pebble feet. Its stone is gently faceted and matte, never metallic. Preserve that ochre parent rock visibly as most of every evolved body. It naturally grows truly precious-looking colorful mineral inclusions and crystals; these are PART OF ITS GEOLOGY, rooted deeply in the rock with visible small mineral growth transitions, not jewelry glued on.
Cell 1 base: match reference untouched.
Cell 2 blade: one broad emerald-green translucent sharp mineral cleavage grows along the left shoulder/body edge as a curved cutting ridge, a small complementary cleavage on right. Crystal edge emerges from body, not a held knife.
Cell 3 piercing: a long tapered amethyst-purple hexagonal crystal prism grows diagonally outward from the upper right body, anchored inside exposed purple mineral seam, not a horn mounted on a headband. A few smaller purple crystal roots, keep face clear.
Cell 4 carapace: dense overlapping low-profile deep sapphire blue crystalline plates grow flush around outer rocky contour, forming a coherent rugged mineral crust with an open ochre face area. Expensive depth and cool reflections, not a necklace.
Cell 5 guard: a single wide polished rose-quartz and warm pink crystal facet expands naturally from the right flank into a thick broad protective buttress, base fused into brown parent rock. Avoid a heraldic shield outline or hand grip.
Cell 6 secretion: small amber and honey-orange translucent geodes open in natural fissures on the upper back and sides, with two heavy tiny glossy resin/mineral-solution droplets at the pores. Give amber inner chambers depth; no potion bottle, no vines. No spikes for this role.
Keep variation restrained and tactile, precious gem color variation intentional but host remains immediately the original pebble species.

SPECIES: SPORE MUSHROOM. Reference is a small squat ivory mushroom-stem creature with a large soft coral-red cap, no mouth, two dark oval eyes, tiny ivory feet. Keep its cap-to-stem proportions and original coral/ivory body. Evolved colorful fungal features must be actual soft mushroom tissue, continuous with the cap and mycelium; do not turn it into a plant, a warrior, or a different giant mushroom species. Saturated multicolor spore sacs are allowed, controlled by role, with simple legible clusters.
Cell 1 base: same as reference.
Cell 2 blade: cap margin naturally grows into three thin sharp sweeping coral-magenta fungal lamellae, particularly along one side like a slicing bracket-fungus rim. Gills clearly continuous under cap; these are fungal cutting edges, NOT metal blades.
Cell 3 piercing: two or three stiff slender indigo-violet fungal stroma grow from the cap's upper outer side, one dominant tapered forward-pointing spear-like hyphal growth, matching living fungus texture. No separate held weapon.
Cell 4 carapace: existing cap becomes thicker, low and dense with three overlapping concentric terracotta and cream bracket-fungus shelves forming a protective multilayer cap; original eyes and stem visible, warm matte fungus texture, no stone armor.
Cell 5 guard: cap grows asymmetrically into one broad drooping turquoise-teal fan of fused small shelf mushrooms on its right side that curls around flank as living fungal shelter. The fan attaches continuously to the main coral cap, a natural mushroom growth, no handle and no round knight shield.
Cell 6 secretion: a few plump spherical translucent spore vesicles grow directly along cap margin in a harmonious rainbow (cyan, purple, pink, gold, lime), with a pair of bright small secretion beads. Sacs are embedded and fused into fungal flesh with coral bases; no bottles, bouquets, jewels or loose bubbles. Cap retains coral parent color and simple silhouette.
All are charming believable fungus evolution, not costumes. Resist extra face details and excessive clusters.

SPECIES: SPRING WATER DROP. The reference is a smooth cyan-turquoise water droplet creature with a swept teardrop tip, two dark navy round eyes, no mouth, NO FEET, no limbs. Every adaptation must change the shape and surface tension of its whole WATER BODY. No attached separate objects, no stone shell, no ice equipment. Maintain luminous watery cyan interior, soft cool aqua highlight upper left, deeper teal lower rim, same eyes and adorable face. Polygonal water bodies are the design vocabulary: softly bulged planar facets and crisp liquid corners, clear water material rather than a cut gemstone or ice block. One continuous volume with gentle surface tension corners. Small controlled accent hues may be inside the water, never jewelry.
Cell 1 base: exact smooth reference drop.
Cell 2 blade: whole water body deforms into a low asymmetrical TRIANGULAR droplet with one thin swept lateral upper edge that forms a continuous cutting fin, still cute and thick-bodied, no appendage blade glued to side.
Cell 3 piercing: elongated triangular/arrowhead water body with one long sharp apex leaning upper right and a sturdy rounded lower face mass; the entire drop converges into the point. One water volume, no spear.
Cell 4 carapace: broad compact OCTAGONAL water body with eight clear rounded polygon corners and a dense doubled liquid rim, as if internal pressure makes a thick protective skin, no scales or plates. Keep watery center cyan, navy eyes.
Cell 5 guard: wider PENTAGONAL water body with high broad shoulders and flattened protective outer front face, five prominent tension corners, dense blue rim; whole silhouette feels sturdy and sheltering. Not a knight shield object.
Cell 6 secretion: rounded six-lobed/HEXAGONAL cyan water body with shallow pores built into three corners and tiny rich blue/cyan droplets budding directly from its own surface. One or two droplets almost pinched off at rim, not bubbles floating over head. Body still reads as fluid polygon, not octopus.
Across all six change actual body geometry decisively; no accessories. Avoid ice spikes, diamond jewelry, extra faces, hands, ground puddles, decorative effects.

SPECIES: SPROUT BEAN. Reference is a pale cream-green plump round bean creature with two big green-black eyes, tiny pale green feet, and one small stem with exactly two soft green leaves. Keep its lovable soft body, eyes, no mouth. Combat growths are its OWN leaves, shoots, seed coat, and nectar glands, with natural shared branching and blended green bases. No wood handles, no man-made objects, no straps. Evolved leaves remain soft painted living green but have distinct functional forms.
Cell 1 base: original two-leaf sprout bean matching reference.
Cell 2 blade: original crown branches into a pair of long asymmetrical sickle-edged dark green leaves that extend naturally down beside the body, with sharp smooth leaf margins and clear continuous stems. Two or three small companion leaves. Not holding leaf swords; the leaves are body growths.
Cell 3 piercing: crown evolves into one tall stiff pointed folded leaf lance leaning upper right, a thick pale green midrib growing directly from the crown with two short supporting young shoots. Keep tiny feet and cream body; avoid cactus spikes all over.
Cell 4 carapace: large thick succulent seed leaves overlap around outer body as a snug living seed coat, three or four broad layered pale-to-deep-green plates with soft fleshy waxy shading. Face remains uncovered, original crown becomes a compact cluster of small leaves. No armor suit, no basket-weave.
Cell 5 guard: one very broad cupped mature leaf fans organically from the side stem and hugs right flank as a continuous living protective canopy; left crown branches into three small leaves. Explore TWO additional tiny dark eyes placed close to the original pair to imply evolution: four total eyes arranged naturally and symmetrically, still friendly, absolutely no horror or many-eye texture. Broad simple shape readable small.
Cell 6 secretion: crown branches into three short stems with plump closed green nectar buds, tiny warm golden dewdrops bead at their tips; buds are not flowers, no petals and no healer motifs. One leaf pair persists below. Pale green tiny pores on upper side of bean connect to nectar stems. No potion containers.
Make this a family of the same bean naturally evolving, cute and surprising, not mutated horror. All skin and plant transitions smooth, no visible sockets.
